one_liner: Run U.S. Cyber Command's internal publications and policy program: review draft instructions, train staff, track updates, and support legal discovery processes.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills suit the training, coordination, and stakeholder parts of this job. The core requirement, though, is one year of specialized experience managing a publications or directives program and reviewing issuances for compliance, and nothing on file shows that yet. A Top Secret clearance requirement adds another hurdle.
eligibility: Who may apply lists 'public', but the text says only applicants meeting specific employment authority categories qualify, with proof documents; confirm which category Daniel fits as a U.S. citizen with no prior federal service.
One year of specialized experience is required: analyzing publications, policies, and directives for compliance, managing a publications program, coordinating reviews, and developing SOPs.
Education cannot substitute for experience; Daniel must qualify on experience alone.
A Top Secret clearance is required; Daniel must be able to obtain one.
This is a Cyber Excepted Service position, so the two-page resume limit does not apply; the full resume must be uploaded as 'Other Documents'.
keywords: instructions, guides, manuals, and policy memoranda
strategy: Apply in the narrow window, October 29 to November 5, 2026. Build the resume in advance and upload the full version under 'Other Documents', since the two-page limit is waived here.

Frame the IEM work around any document tasks you actually did. Examples include reviewing or drafting emergency plans, SOPs, guidance, or after-action reports for compliance with FEMA or client policy, and managing document version control or libraries.

Mirror the specialized-experience language closely. Give a separate bullet each for reviewing documents for accuracy and compliance, maintaining current publications, coordinating stakeholder reviews, and building SOPs, with dates and hours per week.
Highlight your training and outreach strengths, since the job includes training action officers and conducting staff visits.
Answer the questionnaire honestly, rating yourself 'expert' only where the resume backs it up. The posting warns that inflated qualifications cost consideration.
Gather proof-of-eligibility documents for your employment authority category before the job opens.
resume_bullets: Reviewed and edited [number] [emergency operations plans/SOPs/guidance documents] for [client] against [FEMA/state/client] requirements for accuracy, completeness, and compliance; [hours/week], [dates].
Maintained [document library/repository] of [number] plans and policies, tracking revision cycles to keep publications current and accessible to [audience].
Coordinated document reviews with [number] stakeholders across [agencies/offices] and trained [number] staff on [process/SOP], resulting in [result, if known].
interview_questions: Describe a time you reviewed a policy or procedural document for compliance. What did you find, and how did you resolve it?
How would you keep a large set of publications current when action officers miss update deadlines?
How would you train staff who see publications compliance as a low priority?
Tell us about developing or improving an SOP.
watch_outs: The specialized experience is very specific to publications and directives management; if IEM work did not involve that, Daniel may be rated ineligible.
Top Secret clearance and Fort Meade location: about an hour or more from Manassas each way, with telework only partial.
The posting says 'public' but limits applicants to employment authority categories, so verify eligibility before investing time.
The application window is only one week.
